## Summary

remacs stores out-of-fixnum integers as inline `i128` (AGENTS.md: "no bignums"). Results at or above 2^127 do not signal a consistent error. Depending on the operation they become floats, signal `overflow-error`, or print a wrong integer. GNU Emacs has arbitrary-precision bignums, so all of these are exact there.

The worst case is silent wrong output: `(format "%d" (expt 2 130))` prints `170141183460469231731687303715884105727`, which is i128::MAX, not 2^130.

## Reproduction

`remacs --batch -Q --eval '(print (expt 2 130))'`, etc.

| form | GNU Emacs 31.1 | remacs (47792a9) |
|---|---|---|
| `(expt 2 127)` | `170141183460469231731687303715884105728` | `1.7014118346046923e+38` (float) |
| `(expt 3 100)` | `515377520732011331036461129765621272702107522001` | `5.153775207320113e+47` |
| `(1+ (expt 2 127))` | `170141183460469231731687303715884105729` | `1.7014118346046923e+38` |
| `(type-of (expt 2 130))` | `integer` | `float` |
| `(bignump (expt 2 130))` | `t` | `nil` |
| `(format "%d" (expt 2 130))` | `"1361129467683753853853498429727072845824"` | `"170141183460469231731687303715884105727"` (**wrong value, no error**) |
| `(format "%x" (expt 2 130))` | `"400000000000000000000000000000000"` | `"7fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff"` (**wrong value**) |
| `(number-to-string (expt 2 130))` | `"1361129467683753853853498429727072845824"` | `"1.361129467683754e+39"` |
| `(read "1000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000")` | integer 10^45 | `1e+45` (float) |
| `(string-to-number "340282366920938463463374607431768211456")` | integer 2^128 | `3.402823669209385e+38` |
| `(ash 1 127)` | `170141183460469231731687303715884105728` | `(overflow-error 1)` |
| `(* most-positive-fixnum most-positive-fixnum most-positive-fixnum)` | `12259964326927110850916040267783483001021757281745764351` | `(overflow-error 2305843009213693951)` |
| `(let ((r 1)) (dotimes (i 40) (setq r (* r (1+ i)))) r)` (40!) | `815915283247897734345611269596115894272000000000` | `(overflow-error 34)` |
| `(= (expt 2 130) (* (expt 2 65) (expt 2 65)))` | `t` | `(overflow-error 36893488147419103232)` |
| `(% (expt 2 128) 7)` | `4` | `(wrong-type-argument integer-or-marker-p 3.402823669209385e+38)` |
| `(logcount (1- (expt 2 130)))` | `130` | `(wrong-type-argument integerp 1.361129467683754e+39)` |
| `(truncate 1e40)` | `10000000000000000303786028427003666890752` | `(overflow-error 1e+40)` |
| `(random (expt 2 130))` | a non-negative integer below 2^130 | `-525573020410582217` (**negative**) |

The same applies to `floor`/`round`/`ceiling` of large floats, `lognot`/`logand`/`logior` on large values, `mod`, `max`, `abs`, and so on.

## Expected

Integer arithmetic matches GNU at any magnitude, which needs arbitrary-precision integers. At minimum, results that don't fit should never come back as a different integer (`format "%d"`/`"%x"`) or as a negative `random`. Arithmetic overflow should behave the same way across operations, instead of switching between float, `overflow-error` and `wrong-type-argument`.

Calc, `cl-lib` number functions, `bignum` tests in ERT, crypto/hash helpers (e.g. `sha1`-style arithmetic in Lisp), `time-convert` with large `HZ`, etc. all depend on this.
title: Integers >= 2^127 silently become floats / wrong values / overflow-error (no arbitrary-precision bignums)

body:
## Summary

49 variables that are special (dynamically scoped) in GNU Emacs 31.1 are bound in remacs but `special-variable-p` returns nil. Under `lexical-binding: t`, a `let` of any of them creates a lexical binding, so code reading the global value (C code or other functions) never sees the new value. The binding is silently ignored.

`defvaralias` also leaves both the alias and its base variable non-special. GNU's `Fdefvaralias` sets `declared_special` on both.

## Reproduction

Save as `repro.el` (the first line enables lexical binding) and run `remacs --batch -Q -l repro.el` and `emacs --batch -Q -l repro.el`:

```elisp
;;; -*- lexical-binding: t -*-
(print (let ((scroll-step 5)) (symbol-value 'scroll-step)))
(print (let ((text-quoting-style 'grave)) (format-message "`foo'")))
(print (let ((read-process-output-max 1234)) (symbol-value 'read-process-output-max)))
(print (let ((find-file-hooks '(foo))) (symbol-value 'find-file-hook)))
(print (progn (defvaralias 'zz-alias 'zz-base)
              (list (special-variable-p 'zz-alias) (special-variable-p 'zz-base))))
(print (progn (defvar my-base 1) (defvaralias 'my-alias 'my-base)
              (let ((my-alias 2)) my-base)))
```

| form | GNU Emacs 31.1 | remacs (47792a9) |
|---|---|---|
| `(let ((scroll-step 5)) (symbol-value 'scroll-step))` | `5` | `0` |
| `(let ((text-quoting-style 'grave)) (format-message "`foo'"))` | ``"`foo'"`` | `"‘foo’"` |
| `(let ((read-process-output-max 1234)) (symbol-value 'read-process-output-max))` | `1234` | `65536` |
| `(let ((find-file-hooks '(foo))) (symbol-value 'find-file-hook))` | `(foo)` | `(vc-refresh-state epa-file-find-file-hook)` |
| `(defvaralias 'zz-alias 'zz-base)` then `special-variable-p` on both | `(t t)` | `(nil nil)` |
| `(defvar my-base 1) (defvaralias 'my-alias 'my-base) (let ((my-alias 2)) my-base)` | `2` | `1` |

`setq` on the same variables works, because only `let`/`let*` binding is affected.

## Affected variables

I got this list by collecting every bound symbol with `special-variable-p` = t in `emacs -Q --batch` (3516 symbols) and checking each one in `remacs --batch -Q`. All 3516 are bound in remacs, but these 49 are not special:

<details>
<summary>49 variables</summary>

```
after-focus-change-function
clear-message-function
clone-indirect-buffer-hook
comp-enable-subr-trampolines
display-mm-dimensions-alist
edit-abbrevs-map
eldoc-documentation-function
emacs-bzr-version
even-window-heights
find-file-hooks
focus-in-hook
focus-out-hook
fringe-cursor-alist
fringe-indicator-alist
help-enable-auto-load
indicate-unused-lines
inhibit-nul-byte-detection
inhibit-splash-screen
internal--get-default-lexical-binding-function
isearch-lazy-highlight-word
isearch-new-word
isearch-word
jit-lock-defer-contextually
last-input-event
latin-extra-code-table
lisp-font-lock-keywords
lisp-font-lock-keywords-1
lisp-font-lock-keywords-2
messages-buffer-max-lines
minibuffer-mode-map
native-comp-deferred-compilation
ns-version-string
overriding-terminal-local-map
quit-flag
read-process-output-max
real-last-command
region-extract-function
revert-buffer-in-progress-p
scroll-step
set-message-function
standard-display-table
text-quoting-style
throw-on-input
truncate-partial-width-windows
uniquify-after-kill-buffer-p
uniquify-trailing-separator-p
window-safe-min-height
window-safe-min-width
write-file-hooks
```

</details>

Several of these are obsolete aliases (`find-file-hooks`, `write-file-hooks`, `isearch-word`, `messages-buffer-max-lines`, ...), which follows from the `defvaralias` bug. The others are C `DEFVAR_*` variables (`quit-flag`, `throw-on-input`, `text-quoting-style`, `scroll-step`, ...) or Lisp `defvar`/`defconst`s whose values come from the builtin defaults table, so no `defvar` ever marks them special.

## Pointers

- `src/lisp/builtins/data.rs` `f_defvaralias` never sets `.special = true`, on either the alias or the base symbol.
- `src/lisp/eval.rs`: the hand-maintained `specials` list (just before `for name in &specials { ... .special = true }`) is missing the C-level names above. Many of them get their default values from the builtin defaults table in the same function, but they are not marked special there.
title: 49 GNU special variables are not special; defvaralias does not mark alias/base special (let-binding silently ignored under lexical-binding)
